findings.finding: The Q3 adjusted-EPS bar is $0.59 (16 analysts). The CFO said on the 2026-07-28 call that H2 adjusted EPS should be 'near $1.00', split evenly between Q3 and Q4, which puts Q3 near $0.50. FY consensus of $3.22 is likewise above the $3.00-3.10 guide. So the street already expects Polaris to beat its own Q3 number by about $0.09, and a print at the guide would read as a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Polaris beat its own targets in Q1'26 (adj EPS $0.13, well above) and in Q2'26 (operational $1.01 against a $0.70-0.80 target). The stock went +8.88% on Q1 and -4.16% on Q2 despite the beat and raise. Q3'25 ($0.41 vs $0.37 consensus) went -5.31%. Beats were sold on 2 of the last 3 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap between consensus and the company's implied Q3 is visible to anyone who reads the transcript. The market has partly absorbed it through the October target cuts. If consensus had been reset to the guide, the Q3 estimate would sit near $0.50, not $0.59, and FY near $3.05, not $3.22.
findings.independence: Consensus comes from AAII/Zacks, 2026-10-26 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/521347-what-you-need-to-know-about-polaris-incs-q3-earnings), and Benzinga's $0.59 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PII/earnings-forecasts). The guide is a separate document (the transcript).

findings.finding: Polaris kept 'about $40 million' of further IEEPA refunds out of FY guidance 'because there is not currently a formal process to apply for the next phase'. CBP's CAPE Phase 3, which covers finally liquidated entries under court-ordered reliquidation, deployed on 2026-10-06, and the CIT certified an IEEPA refund class action on 2026-10-08. The call can therefore plausibly add roughly $0.50-0.55 of adjusted EPS ($40M pre-tax, ~23% tax, ~56.5M shares) to the FY guide. Polaris books refunds only when received, so the cash is a Q4 item, and it is not certain Polaris qualifies for Phase 3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2'26 print included a $74M refund ($0.96 of adjusted EPS) that lifted FY adjusted guidance from $1.60-1.70 to $3.00-3.10. The stock fell 4.16%, so the market looked through the refund-driven raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY of $3.22 sits only ~$0.12-0.22 above the guide, less than the ~$0.5 the excluded refund would add, so the street carries at most part of it. The Phase 3 launch is a customs-broker advisory that the analysts' October notes are not reported to have discussed. If it were priced, FY consensus would sit near $3.5.
findings.independence: C.H. Robinson advisory on Phase 3 (deploys 2026-10-06, effective 2026-09-17): https://www.chrobinson.com/en-sg/resources/insights-and-advisories/client-advisories/2026q3/09-17-26-cbp-cape-phase-3-ieepa-refunds/ ; CIT class certification on 2026-10-08: https://www.rvia.org/news-insights/court-international-trade-certifies-class-action-ieepa-tariff-refund-lawsuit . The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/931015/000162828026050104/pii-20260630.htm) shows an $83.0M IEEPA receivable at 2026-06-30. Eligibility for Phase 3 (plaintiffs with court-ordered reliquidation) is unconfirmed for Polaris; I found no Polaris CIT filing.

findings.finding: Third-quarter demand evidence is flat, with a competitor taking share. BRP (reported 2026-09-03, after Polaris last spoke): North American side-by-side retail up mid-single digits against low-single-digit industry growth, current-model-year SSV share up more than 3 points to a record, and a tougher Q3 expected. CDK Lightspeed data across 1,700+ dealers: same-store sales -0.8%, major units +0.2%. University of Michigan sentiment -11.2% y/y in August. Polaris's own H2 plan already assumes 'flattish' retail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ORV retail and share comments have driven the reaction before: Q2'26's +5% ORV retail and share gains still saw the stock sell off. In 2024 weak ORV retail drove large drops.
findings.why_not_priced: BRP's share-gain claim is public. The dealer DMS series is trade-press only, but it is in line with Polaris's own flat-retail assumption, so it mostly lands inside the guide. Sized small, as a proxy.
findings.independence: CDK Lightspeed dealer series (THE SHOP, 2026-09-25): https://theshopmag.com/features/kpi-september-2026-the-brief/ ; MIC/consumer sentiment (2026-09-23): https://powersportsbusiness.com/news/dealers/2026/09/23/new-data-shows-growing-concerns-over-us-economy-could-hurt-powersports-sales/ . Both are proxies, not Polaris numbers.

findings.finding: Sentiment going into the print is washed out. Three target cuts this month: Baird 72->65 (2026-10-07), Wells Fargo 70->55 (2026-10-10), Citi 67->56 (~2026-10-19). The stock is -22.9% since the July print, with 1 Buy / 12 Hold / 1 Sell. Short interest has risen 36% since July to 4.9M shares (8.6% of shares outstanding, 5.2 days to cover). That lowers the bar for the reaction to an in-line print with a held guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26 came in after a drawdown and went +8.88%. Q2'26 came in after a rebound (to $74.6) and went -4.16%. The pattern is consistent with reactions fading the run-in.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself. What it is not pricing is a positive surprise: if it were, the stock would not sit 26% off its high with short interest building. The +6.25% bounce of the last five sessions has already recovered part of it.
findings.independence: Short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/pii/shortinterest (read 2026-10-26). Wells Fargo date: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9129845/pii-maintained-by-wells-fargo-price-target-lowered-to-55 . Price since the print: AAII 2026-10-26.

findings.finding: There is room for constructive 2027 talk on the call. Management guided that the Indian Motorcycle separation (majority sale closed 2026-02-02) adds about $50M of adjusted EBITDA, 'weighted toward January 2027'. The Osceola, WI plant is being closed (WARN notice for 189 workers dated 2026-07-27), with charges excluded from adjusted results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Polaris's Q3 calls rarely give a next-year guide; the Q4 call (January) does. The 2025-10-14 Indian divestiture announcement went +13.92%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is already disclosed; the only new thing would be management quantifying a 2027 bridge on the call. If 2027 accretion were in the price, FY27 estimates would visibly step up, and no source here shows that.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/28/polaris-pii-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) for the $50M figure, which shares a source with finding 1. WARN notice: https://layofftracker.us/layoffs/company/polaris/2026

findings.finding: The balance-sheet question answers to working capital, not distress. Revolver debt rose to $459.8M at 2026-06-30 from $35.4M at year-end, funding a seasonal inventory build ($1,566M, finished goods $683M). Net leverage fell to 2.6x from 3.6x, and the covenant-relief period (5.5x) ended with the 2026-06-30 quarter. Management expected 'strong cash flow conversion as seasonal working capital unwinds' in H2, plus collection of the $83.0M refund receivable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior reaction to a leverage update. H1'26 free cash flow was -$143.7M, against +$343.8M a year earlier.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 cash and leverage are not visible until the print. A Q3 cash inflow from the receivable and the working-capital unwind would show in the reported net leverage.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000931015/000162828026049902/pii-q22026earningsrelease.htm) shares the 10-Q's numbers, so it is not independent.

baseline_tension: Skew is balanced (+0.87) but unusable; the 20-day run-up is +5.6% and the 5-day +6.25%, off a deep drawdown. The findings offset each other and do not cut strongly against either.

Lesson 5 / core (a proxy inside what the company guided moves toward 0): the industry-demand finding went from -0.5 to -0.3, because Polaris's own H2 plan already assumes flat retail.
Lesson 7 / core: the positioning finding went from +0.5 to +0.4, since the 5-day bounce has partly used it up. Short interest is moderate, not crowded.
Core (a known disclosure has a small path to a new number): the 2027 Indian/Osceola finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lesson 1: no change to the reported-quarter finding, since beats sold on 2 of the last 3 prints already support its negative sign. Lesson 4: the financing finding stays at +0.2 because the money funds seasonal working capital and leverage is falling. abs_move_pct and p_up are unchanged.
